surfaces.part: paw-print shapes (five small separate prints, light blue with a white lower edge)

answer.evidence: The image is five small, separate decal shapes, each about 3-4 rows tall, spread across rows 4-13. Each print is 2 rows of light blue (L=185) with 1 row of white (L=215-255) at the bottom, as in the column scans at x=8, 16 and 23. The white row is a highlight on a flat print, not a front face. No part has 3 or more rows of vertical face, no ellipse, no eave shadow and no receding side face. This is a flat floor decal seen from above, which fits the 'flat' kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is not a 4x3 ground patch. It is a tiny sparse cluster of a few pale pixels (about 3 distinct colours) on a dark background, far smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts are 0. By eye it has 2-3 flat tones with no grain, tufts, or soil variation, and no outline structure. The grass reference shows about 3 visible tones with clumps and grain, and the paving reference about 7 with shaded stones. The candidate carries far less information than either and does not read as a ground surface at all. It would look thinner and flatter than the references.

The width profile (rows 4-13, widths 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 7, 9, 1) comes from the diagonal staggering of the prints, not from a volume. This matches the flat kind and reads as a top-down slab with no front face.
